sources.locator: Chapter II, §1.1, Definitions 1.1–1.2 and Definition/Proposition 1.3 with its proof, through Remark 1.5, printed pp. 48–49 (PDF pp. 58–60); smooth-loop and polynomial-loop conventions.
sources.reading_extent: Inspected the complete cited section in the 316-page book PDF, including the smooth-loop domain, invariant-form convention, cocycle formula, central bracket, proof sketch, and Remark 1.5. No claim is made about unrelated chapters.

contents.name: Definition 1.1: smooth loop algebra with pointwise bracket

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete definition and adjacent setup.
source_review.supports: The local definition uses the full smooth mapping space C∞(S¹,g) and pointwise bracket.
source_review.limitations: The source assumes a connected simply connected integrating group elsewhere; the local item only needs the Lie algebra and imposes no group integration assumption.

contents.name: Definition 1.2: invariant bilinear form

source_review.read_extent: Read the exact invariance identity and matrix example.
source_review.supports: The local item states symmetry and the invariant identity explicitly.
source_review.limitations: The source discusses real-valued forms; the local interface fixes a real form and makes no nondegeneracy or positivity assumption.

contents.name: Definition/Proposition 1.3: derivative cocycle and central bracket

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete formula and its adjoining proof paragraph.
source_review.supports: The proposition proves the displayed smooth-loop cocycle and the resulting central bracket.
source_review.limitations: The book gives only a proof sketch for the cyclic identity; the local item supplies the complete calculation.

contents.name: Proof of Definition/Proposition 1.3: integration by parts and invariance

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the complete source proof paragraph and adjacent Exercise 1.4.
source_review.supports: The source identifies the periodic integration-by-parts and invariant-form steps used locally.
source_review.limitations: The local proof expands every cyclic term and independently checks Jacobi and exactness of the sequence.

contents.name: Remark 1.5: polynomial-loop restriction and simple-algebra uniqueness
contents.reason: The assigned definition uses all smooth loops and permits any symmetric invariant form; polynomial-loop classification and uniqueness for simple g are not required by this interface.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete remark, including its Laurent-polynomial residue convention and simplicity qualification.
source_review.supports: Clarifies the relation between the smooth loop formula, its polynomial-loop restriction, and the narrower simple-algebra convention.
source_review.limitations: The local definition deliberately does not restrict g to be simple or κ to be nondegenerate, and makes no classification or quantization claim.

contents.name: Proof 4: cyclic residue identity

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete product-rule and cancellation argument.
source_review.supports: Corroborates the cyclic 2-cocycle calculation.

contents.name: Proposition 3: one-dimensional central extension bracket

sources.title: Adel Bilal, Lectures on Anomalies
sources.locator: §7.1, §9.1–9.2, and §11.3.2, PDF pp. 45–49, 70–72, and 92–93; chiral trace coefficients, Wess–Zumino/BRST consistency and the four-dimensional mixed gauge-gravitational term.
sources.reading_extent: Inspected the complete cited equations and their adjacent derivations: the representation trace and chirality sum, the Wess–Zumino-to-BRST relation and local counterterm equivalence, and the 4D mixed polynomial. The 108-page lecture text is not claimed read outside these sections.

contents.name: §7.1, equation (7.1): symmetrized cubic representation trace

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete trace definition and its chirality-sign discussion.
source_review.supports: Supports the cubic trace interface and makes the generator symmetrization convention explicit.
source_review.limitations: The source uses a symmetrized trace with a factor convention; the local statement defines the no-half anticommutator and records the conversion.

contents.name: §7.1, equations (7.8)–(7.9): left-handed fields and charge-conjugate right-handed antiparticles

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete charge-conjugation and representation-transpose calculation.
source_review.supports: Supports interpreting a vectorlike U(1) pair as left-handed charges q and −q.
source_review.limitations: The example proves only the trace arithmetic; it imports no dynamical cancellation theorem.

contents.name: §9.1: Wess–Zumino consistency for a gauge variation of the effective action

source_review.read_extent: Read the full displayed consistency derivation from closure of gauge generators.
source_review.supports: Supports the definition of a local consistent anomaly as an infinitesimal Ward variation obeying the gauge-algebra consistency condition.
source_review.limitations: The local item retains locality and the specific regulated effective action as hypotheses.

contents.name: §9.2, equations (9.10)–(9.15): BRST closure and local-counterterm equivalence

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete passage deriving BRST closure and explaining local counterterm equivalence.
source_review.supports: Supports the H¹(s|d) interpretation used to delimit the local obstruction interface.
source_review.limitations: The source’s model-specific Ward and regularization context is not generalized into an unproved claim by this definition.

contents.name: §11.3.2, equations (11.29)–(11.31): four-dimensional mixed gauge-gravitational coefficient

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete 4D index-polynomial expansion and U(1) linear-trace specialization.
source_review.supports: Supports tracking the linear trace coefficient separately from the cubic gauge tensor.
source_review.limitations: Curvature, chirality, generator and numerical normalization conventions remain explicit inputs to any later model theorem.
